subject: EdgeHealth inference evaluation — playbook & scoring rubric
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgehealth.ai>, Samir Dutta <samir@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeHealth inference evaluation — playbook & scoring rubric

Hi Alex / Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed playbook so we can move the comparison to a technical POC quickly. I pasted the short plan below and attached a one‑page playbook (edgehealth_eval_playbook_v1.docx).

Summary of ask from your side:
- Compare Redwood hosted and dedicated inference against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned (AWS Bedrock + managed OpenAI style API) for a subset of production flows (clinical summarization + triage).
- Validate latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, and output fidelity on your sample data.
- Confirm integration constraints (VPC peering / data retention / SOC2 evidence) before any dedicated infra is provisioned.

Proposed POC playbook (owners and rough timeline):
1) Define test corpus & scoring (owner: Alex + Redwood lead) — deadline: Jun 22
2) Run baseline runs against hyperscalers (owner: Marcus) — Jun 29 to Jul 2
3) Redwood runs + optimizations (quantization/batching) (owner: Marcus + Jordan) — Jul 3 to Jul 6
4) Human eval for fidelity / safety / hallucination rate (owner: Alex + Samir, with Redwood facilitating) — Jul 7 to Jul 9
5) Scorecard and recommend next step (owner: Vanessa) — Jul 10

Success criteria (example):
- p95 tail latency < 450ms for 512 token prompts for 95% of test cases (or parity with hyperscaler)
- Cost per 1k tokens within 20% of best hyperscaler observed for comparable latency tier
- Human fidelity score >= baseline (manual scoring rubric attached in playbook)
- No blocking security gaps (VPC, KMS integration, audit logs)

Open questions for EdgeHealth (can you confirm by EOD Tue?):
- Who will be primary test contact and who owns procurement?
- Do you require a private VPC deployment for the POC or is hosted with strict retention acceptable for now?

Next immediate asks from Redwood
- Please provide a 200–500 case sample (anonymized) and a short list of golden outputs you use for fidelity checks. Attachment accepted via secure upload or SFTP.
- Confirm a 2‑hour window in the week of Jun 29 for baseline runs — we recommend morning Pacific.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate infra reservations once you confirm the sample and the procurement contact.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgehealth_eval_playbook_v1.docx (docx)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@edgehealth.ai>

Subject: Re: EdgeHealth inference evaluation — playbook & scoring rubric

Thanks Vanessa — useful summary. Quick answers:
- Primary test contact: me (Alex Morgan). Procurement: procurement@edgehealth.org (procurement team). I’ve CC’d Samir (PM) to help assemble sample data and the golden outputs.
- For the POC we prefer hosted to get started, but we will likely require a VPC option if we see data residency concerns in the SOC review. Either way we want to run the initial comparison as you outlined.

Tentative availability: we can take the baseline run window on Jun 30 09:00–11:00 PT. Samir will upload an anonymized 300‑case CSV to the secure upload link by Jun 22.

Can you include a short manifest of the exact input/output schema we should provide? Also please send the scoring rubric (even a simple template) so our clinicians know how to mark fidelity.

— Alex
Head of Product, EdgeHealth
alex.morgan@edgehealth.ai

Alex / Vanessa — looping in a terse tech plan and deliverables so your team has clarity on owners and artifacts. I attached a test_manifest.csv that lists input fields and expected outputs.

Technical test plan (short):
- Benchmarks: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, RAM/GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens (billing simulated at Redwood hosted rates). We will record perf under identical sequence lengths and batch sizes.
- Models & variants: Redwood-curated model X-3B (FP16), quantized X-3B (8-bit), and an MPT-style baseline we use for fast low-latency runs. Hyperscaler runs will be scripted against the endpoints you provided.
- Fidelity: we will produce model outputs and collect human ratings (1–5) across clarity, clinical safety, and relevance. Please include your clinicians in the rating step (we will provide the Google Sheet).
- Security checks: VPC peering feasibility, KMS key exchange, and retention policy compliance (owner: Neha).

Owners / contacts: Marcus — test harness, cluster reservations, and cost accounting; Neha — security & compliance questionnaire and VPC gating; Vanessa — commercial lead and scorecard signoff.

Schedule (confirmed windows):
- Jun 22: dataset + golden outputs deadline (EdgeHealth)
- Jun 29–30: hyperscaler baseline runs (Marcus)
- Jul 1–3: Redwood runs & optimization iterations (Marcus + Jordan)
- Jul 6–9: human eval (EdgeHealth + Redwood)
- Jul 10: scorecard & decision call (all)

Quick asks from your side: please confirm the exact schema (we attached test_manifest.csv) and provide a sample of tokenized inputs if you can. We’ll also need any rate limits your data ingest pipeline has so we can mirror.

Calendar: I put the Jun 30 09:00 slot on Vanessa’s calendar — accept if OK.

— Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
